title: While the mind still works
hookLine: hurry, not only because death nears, but because understanding may fail first (Meditations 3.1)

cards: Watching a grandparent slowly lose their memory can bring a particular kind of sadness. The hands are still there, the laugh, the way they hold a cup.

But the person who could tell you the story, or say the thing you were waiting to hear, is harder and harder to reach. Book three opens with a short note in the manuscripts: at Carnuntum, a fortress on the Danube.
Then Marcus looks straight at that possibility for himself. Today: while the mind still works.

teach.b: Each day, Marcus begins, life is spent, and less of it remains. We've heard that from him, and from Seneca. Then he adds something new.
Even if a person lives longer, it isn't certain the mind will stay able to understand things, to think about what's human and what's divine. Breathing, eating, imagining, wanting: those may carry on.
What can go first is the power to use ourselves well: to see our duties clearly, to sort out appearances, to think something through. So, he says, we must hurry.

Not only because death comes closer every day, but because understanding may stop before life does. It matters how we hear that. This isn't a judgment on anyone whose mind has changed with age or illness.
A person's worth doesn't leave with their memory, and the people who care for them know it. Marcus is talking to himself, about timing.

If something needs a clear mind, don't assume the clear mind will always be there: the letter to your children, the hard conversation, the will, the forgiveness, the thing you keep saying you'll learn.
Even the talks with the older people you love, while they can still tell you the story.

teach.h: WHAT NEEDS A CLEAR MIND, DO NOW.
teach.b: The urgency isn't panic. It's the steady push this path keeps meeting: now, not someday. Marcus just adds one more reason.
Not only while I live. While I can.

how: Some readers take this entry as a push to stop postponing tasks that need clear thinking, such as important letters, plans and conversations with older relatives.

games.q: what does “while the mind still works” mean?
o: only the young can think clearly about the big questions
doing what needs a clear mind now, before the mind may fade
keeping your mind sharp with puzzles as you grow older

games.q: while the mind still works — tap the pairs.

s: Marcus says a person's worth depends on their mind staying sharp
he's talking to himself about timing, not judging anyone's worth.
Marcus gives two reasons to hurry: death, and the mind failing first
that second reason is new in book three.
Marcus wrote book three in retirement in Rome
a note places it at Carnuntum, a fortress on the Danube.

games.q: you've meant for years to ask your grandmother about her childhood. she's still sharp, but getting older. what fits Meditations 3.1?
o: wait for a holiday visit next year.
call this week, while you both can.
games.why: understanding may fail before life does, Marcus says. so hurry.

practice: Notice that your mind is working right now, following words, holding a thought, and let that be a small wonder for a moment.
Then think of one thing that needs this clear mind, something you've been putting off: a letter, a decision, a question for an older relative. Picture yourself doing it, while you can.

wordCard.voice: While the mind still works. Marcus says hurry, not only because death nears, but because understanding may fail before life does. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: understanding, the thinking mind. What Marcus says may fail before life does.

carryVoice: Your line: while I can. Not only while I live, while the mind is clear. See you tomorrow.
